arc_two_years_of_paper.turn_in_text:
It's been two years.

I'm going to read this properly, and then I'm going to put it on the wall of the longhouse, where everyone who's still angry about it can see the date on it. Thank you for carrying it. Go and see the Quartermaster.

org_binding_invoker.description: Malzhet has spent a lifetime learning where a warlock's contract ends. Jergosh the Invoker has built a chamber in the chasm, and a cult round the idea that it never ends at all. Voidwalkers he didn't earn walk his ritual hall. Malzhet recognises the mistake, because he made it himself twenty years ago, and he doesn't want to see it made again on the scale of a city.
org_binding_invoker.accept_text: The way down is Ragefire Chasm, in the south-west corner of the city, a long walk from my door. Inside, Jergosh's chamber lies north of the lake. Mind the Voidwalker Minions, because they're his hands, and he's never once had to use his own. When he falls, break the circle, and don't read what's in it.
org_binding_invoker.turn_in_text:
The circle's broken, so the debt's paid, at least in part.

Take this with you. A better warlock than me used to carry it, and I'd be pleased if you turned out better than either of us.

org_cinderfang.description: Rethok doesn't hunt for sport. He hunts what threatens the herd, and a salamander the size of a wolf has taken to the shores of the lava lake beneath the city. The troggs call it Cinderfang, and they keep their distance. Rethok keeps a list of the animals he's failed to bring home, and the list is short.
org_cinderfang.accept_text: The lake's in Ragefire Chasm, and the way in is the south-west corner of the city. It lairs on the north-east shore. The Cinder Salamanders will lead you to it, because they're always near a bigger one. Keep to the stone, don't touch the lava, and don't run.
org_cinderfang.turn_in_text:
That's a clean kill. I've seen that pelt on a trogg's wall once, and I won't again.

Choose whichever piece you'll use. I'd only hang it on a wall.

org_embers_beneath.description: The warm vents under the Cleft of Shadow used to be only warm. For a month now they've been loud with picks and drums, and there's a smell of sulphur that doesn't belong to nature. Troggs who haven't come near the city in a generation are streaming up out of Ragefire Chasm, and something with a purpose is behind them. Thrall doesn't like things with a purpose he hasn't given them.
org_embers_beneath.accept_text: Go down through the Cleft. Kill the Ragefire Troggs first, because they're the loud part, and the Ragefire Shamans who keep them loud. Then come back and tell me what the chasm has become. I won't send a tide of warriors into a place I don't understand.
org_embers_beneath.turn_in_text:
So it isn't only troggs. I'd rather know that than not, and the Cleft's quieter already.

But something down below is feeding that fire. Take this, and listen to me again.

org_hexed_ash.description: The Searing Blade doesn't burn its offerings for flavour. The ash is a reagent, the reagent is a curse, and a curse needs a hand. Zurm has spent a week analysing the ash his customers brought back, and every sample points the same way: down the chasm, to a priestess called Zhurra Bloodhex.
org_hexed_ash.turn_in_text:
I won't ask what you saw. I'll say that the sample matches, and her curse is broken at the root.

I'd like you to have something from my own stock.

org_hunger_in_the_lake.description: The cultists didn't find the lava lake. They found what lives in it. Taragaman the Hungerer is an elemental older than the city, and for ten thousand years he's done nothing but burn and wait. Someone has been feeding him, binding him, and pointing him at Orgrimmar. A bound spirit of that size is a fuse waiting to be lit.
org_hunger_in_the_lake.turn_in_text:
The Hungerer's gone. I felt the vents go quiet from here, and for the first time in a month the city's breathing right.

There's still the one who held his chain.

org_ore_deep.description: Krunk keeps one piece of black rock above his anvil, and he's been staring at it for a week. It came from the mining spur under the Cleft, and it's the best ore he's ever put a hammer to. He wants more. In his view, the troggs digging it up and the elementals warming it down below are a very small obstacle.
org_ore_deep.accept_text: It's down in Ragefire Chasm, south of my forge, in the corner where the city wall meets the rock. Troggs mine it and elementals nest in it. Bring me lumps of it, black and shot with orange. You'll know it when you pick it up, because it'll want to burn your hand.
org_ore_deep.turn_in_text:
Look at that grain. I could make a blade from this that would sing, and though it won't be today, I won't forget who brought it.

Here's something from the racks.

org_pitbreaker.description: The best ore in the spur belongs to a trogg called Grulgash. He isn't a warlord. He's a miner with a miner's grudge, and a hammer that's broken more pit-props than Krunk has forged blades. Nobody mines the black seam while Grulgash is breathing, and Krunk would pay a fair bit to see that change.
org_pitbreaker.accept_text: Go back down Ragefire Chasm, south of my forge. Inside, he's west of the warrens, past the supply racks. Kill the Ragefire Diggers first, because they keep him informed. Grulgash is bigger than he looks and angrier than he sounds.
org_pitbreaker.turn_in_text:
The seam's open, and I'll have the smiths down there before the week's out.

As for his hammer, I don't need it, and you do. Choose whatever you want from the racks.

org_sinister_edge.description: Every cult needs a blade, and the Searing Blade's is a trogg-hater named Bazzalan. He sits on an obsidian throne at the end of the chasm, in a hall that was an orc shrine before it was theirs. He doesn't shout and he doesn't pose. He waits for you to look at the wrong corner of the room.
org_sinister_edge.turn_in_text:
You did more than bring his throne to dust. The Searing Blade's hold on my city is broken, at least for now.

Wear this with pride. The Horde remembers who stands in the dark so that others can sleep.

org_whispers_cleft.description: The Cleft of Shadow has always belonged to the quiet kind of orc. That doesn't mean it belongs to whoever claims the quiet. A cult calling itself the Searing Blade has been using the Cleft's back tunnels to run its ritual stock down into the chasm. The Shade isn't pleased. A thief has a code, and the code doesn't include sacrifices.
org_whispers_cleft.accept_text: They hide behind candlelight, and you can use that. Go in through the gate in the Cleft and take them as they come: the Searing Blade Cultists first, then the Fanatics who guard them, and the Invokers who command them.
org_whispers_cleft.turn_in_text:
Their whispers have gone quiet, and I'll be back to my usual clientele by dusk.

Here's a small thank-you from a very small ghost.

org_who_holds_the_floor.description:
Elder Torgun's report on the southern border now has a second page, and it's worse than the first. There's country beyond the range after all, there are tauren living on top of it, and between the Horde and the salt flats, a people holds the only ground that connects anything to anything.

The Warchief doesn't need their history. He needs their name and their numbers.
org_who_holds_the_floor.accept_text:
They're the Galak, centaur but not Kolkar, a different stock with different manners, and by every account better organised than anything we've fought on this continent.

Go down onto that floor and find out what they're made of. Count the Galak Outriders, and count their Windcatchers separately, because a people who post weather-watchers have a plan.
org_who_holds_the_floor.turn_in_text:
They're drilled, then, and they keep a pace. They don't break and they don't chase.

I'll write that down, and I'll be unpopular for it. Everyone upstairs wants to hear about savages.
